claim: A promote gate is a statistical instrument, not a counter. Feed candidates decision-only feedback (never scores) and split a global error budget alpha across decision histories to certify, with probability >= 1-alpha over the whole run, that every promoted modification is a genuine population improvement (REUSE 2609.33180, verified live this session: naive best-of-K took 75 false promotions, up to 20.7% of accepted updates non-positive; REUSE took 0 at matched final performance within 0.04 pp). Accept on a private held-out grade, then prove generalization on benchmarks never fed back into selection plus a held-out hacking instrument (AIDE2 2609.26457, verified: 99 proposals, 7 accepted, grade 0.703 to 0.778, hacking 55% to 32%, non-monotone across checkpoints so ledgers need per-checkpoint rows). Treat a patched exploit route as unclosed until a fresh alternative-route attempt fails (Unearned Passes 2609.34262, verified: 3,810 passing trajectories audited, violation = mechanism + intent + grade relevance, git_oracle_seal case showed replay closure without channel closure). Run each promotion paired against a frozen baseline with attribution (SEABench 2609.35596, verified: 316/720 evolved safety failures vs 0/720 baseline, Fisher p=3.48e-13, attribution is process-level per its Appendix A, a correction to the find). Spend scarce high-fidelity verification by expected selection-regret reduction per cost (PIVOT-KG 2609.32677, verified: near-zero-MAE verifier still reverses 100% of proposed updates, Leduc 2.5% to 51.7% at eight steps). Wrap promotions in change manifests, fixed regression sets, and rollback with the updater barred from weakening its own acceptance predicate (RegenHarness 2609.27612, verified: protocol only, no experimental RSI results).

claim: Three mechanisms from arXiv 2609.32042 (PolAgentBench, three GGUF k-quant models, Q8_0 to Q2_K). (1) The collapse threshold replicates, the failure mode does not: across a fourfold capability spread and two axes of variation, exactly one thing transfers, the cliff between 3-bit and 2-bit (11B 0.716 to 0.045, 7B 0.463 to 0.149, PLLuM 0.224 to 0.015, paired McNemar p<0.001 each), so a quant floor must be keyed to role and never learned from one model's telemetry; at 27B the endpoints confirm it (Q4_K_M matches BF16 on agentic Terminal-Bench 2.1, 1-bit collapses to chance, per quesma.com/blog/qwen38-27b-quantizations-benchmarked/). (2) Below the cliff, failure looks like success to a tool harness: 2-bit failures keep the protocol well formed (a final_answer with no parse error and an empty tool log) while confabulating content, 37 of 64 eleven-B failures answer at step one with a confabulated final, and PLLuM keeps parsing 71.8 to 92.0 percent of steps while failing content, so harnesses must score protocol-shape and content separately because parse-success telemetry is blind exactly where the model is most broken. (3) A free zero-inference collapse detector, inverted token economics: at every precision except 11B Q2_K failing trajectories cost MORE tokens than passing ones (1.18x to 7.65x); at 11B Q2_K the failures are the CHEAP ones (median 1,506.5 vs 4,010 tokens) because the model answers before it looks, so steps-to-final, tool-calls-before-final, and tokens-per-trajectory form an alarm that costs nothing at run time. Rider: scaffolding repair is precision-coupled (explicit decomposition lifts 8-bit from 1/10 to 9/10 but does not survive to 4-bit), and per-model failure taxonomies are measured, never assumed.
